articles.title: Banco Master: Crise no STF trava inquérito-mãe da PF sobre fraudes | G1
articles.summary: A Polícia Federal adiou a conclusão do inquérito do Banco Master sobre fraudes de Daniel Vorcaro devido à paralisação do caso provocada por crise no STF.
articles.body:
A Polícia Federal havia planejado fechar, até o fim de setembro, o primeiro inquérito do Banco Master, classificado de inquérito-mãe, que trata das fraudes bancárias praticadas por Daniel Vorcaro.

Contudo, a PF acabou sendo obrigada a mudar de planos depois da crise no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) , que paralisou o caso. Agora, tudo indica que a conclusão vai ficar para depois das eleições, atrasando as investigações de outras etapas do caso.

Os investigadores avaliavam incialmente que seria possível fechar esse primeiro inquérito entre agosto e setembro por considerar que as fraudes bancárias praticadas pelo Banco Master na tentativa de venda da instituição para o BRB, o banco público de Brasília, já estão comprovadas.

Nesta primeira fase, a PF vai pedir o indiciamento do banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro, do ex-presidente do BRB Paulo Henrique Costa e de servidores do Banco Central que ajudaram o dono do Master com informações privilegiadas.

Nesta quarta-feira (30), o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro e seu pai, Henrique Vorcaro, vão depor na Polícia Federal.

Esses depoimentos serão feitos para elucidar a existência do grupo "Turma" , que seria encarregado de fazer ameaças a pessoas classificadas pelo dono do Master como suas adversárias e inimigas.

Os dados do celular trazem informações de algumas tentativas de agressões, até contra jornalistas, pela "turma".

Esse grupo, montado por Daniel Vorcaro, era comandado por Luiz Phillipi Mourão, o Sicário. Preso em uma operação da Polícia Federal, ele acabou tirando a própria vida numa cela do órgão em Belo Horizonte .

O pai dele é apontado como o responsável por fazer pagamentos ao Sicário. Henrique Vorcaro nega qualquer envolvimento no caso .

articles.title: Pablo Marçal anuncia entrada na equipe de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato a presidente pelo PL disse que Marçal vai trabalhar em propostas sobre empreendedorismo. Apesar do anúncio, o partido de Marçal, PRTB, segue com candidatura própria na eleição.
articles.summary: Apesar da entrada na campanha do senador do PL, o partido de Marçal, PRTB, segue com candidato próprio na eleição,
articles.body:
Pablo Marçal (PRTB) anuncia entrada na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) durante agenda de campanha em São Paulo (SP) nesta terça-feira (29) — Foto: Vittor Sales

O empresário Pablo Marçal (PRTB) anunciou que entrou na equipe de campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) para a Presidência da República. O comunicado aconteceu nessa terça-feira (29) em São Paulo.

Em fala a jornalistas numa academia de jiu-jitsu, Flávio disse que Marçal vai desenvolver propostas voltadas ao empreendedorismo e "incentivar uma cultura de prosperidade dentro das famílias, para que não precisem depender de ninguém ou do governo para terem que levar dignidade para suas casas."

"Pablo Marçal está vindo para nos ajudar nessa parte de empreendedorismo e de mobilidade social. É alguém que é um grande empreendedor, e está unindo forças nessa grande coalizão", afirmou Flávio Bolsonaro.

Apesar do ingresso na campanha Flávio, o PRTB, partido de Marçal, segue com candidatura própria à Presidência da República. Após o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) barrar o registro da candidatura de Marçal em setembro , o então vice dele, Leonardo Avalanche , se tornou cabeça de chapa.

Ao lado de Flávio durante o anúncio, Pablo Marçal destacou que seu objetivo é "aposentar Lula". "Um presidenciável vai virar o voto para Flávio ainda nesta semana", disse o empresário.

"Eu cheguei a convite do Flávio e reafirmo a vocês que todos estão contra o PT agora, e é hora de salvar esse país", disse Marçal.

articles.title: TSE manda Nikolas Ferreira apagar publicação que associa fala de Lula a conteúdo sexual envolvendo crianças | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministra Estela Aranha afirmou que deputado descontextualizou declaração sobre prevenção ao câncer de próstata. Publicação deverá ser retirada do X em até 24 horas.
articles.summary: Ministra Estela Aranha afirmou que deputado descontextualizou declaração sobre prevenção ao câncer de próstata. Publicação deverá ser retirada do X em até 24 horas.
articles.body:
A ministra Estela Aranha, do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), determinou nesta quarta-feira (30) que Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) remova, em até 24 horas, uma publicação no X em que associa uma declaração do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) a conteúdo sexual envolvendo crianças e adolescentes.

Na decisão, a ministra afirma que a postagem descontextualizou uma fala de Lula feita durante um discurso sobre prevenção e tratamento do câncer de próstata e sobre a resistência dos homens à realização de exames médicos.

Estela Aranha também determinou que Nikolas se abstenha de republicar ou divulgar novamente o mesmo conteúdo ou mídias "substancialmente idênticas".

O X foi notificado para remover a publicação em até 24 horas e informar à Justiça Eleitoral as providências adotadas ( entenda mais abaixo ).

A decisão é liminar, ou seja, provisória. A própria ministra determinou que o caso seja submetido ao plenário do TSE, inclusive com a possibilidade de análise em sessão virtual.

A ação foi apresentada pela Coligação "Brasil Pronto Pra Mais", que sustenta que Nikolas divulgou, na terça (29), um trecho recortado de uma declaração de Lula e atribuiu à fala uma conotação sexual relacionada a crianças e adolescentes.

Segundo a coligação, a íntegra do discurso mostra que Lula falava sobre a resistência dos homens aos exames preventivos e comparava esse comportamento ao acompanhamento médico realizado por mulheres.

Na publicação questionada, Nikolas contestou essa interpretação e relacionou a declaração do presidente a meninas e a práticas criminosas envolvendo crianças.

Dep. Nikolas Ferreira (PL - MG) — Foto: Kayo Magalhães / Câmara dos Deputados

Na decisão, Estela Aranha afirmou que a publicação de Nikolas vai além de uma crítica política ou de uma discordância sobre a expressão utilizada por Lula.

Segundo ela, o deputado deu à fala uma "conotação inteiramente diversa" da original, retirando a discussão do contexto de saúde pública e associando-a a crimes envolvendo crianças e adolescentes.

"Não se está diante de mera interpretação alternativa de um fato incontroverso, mas de construção discursiva capaz de conduzir o destinatário da mensagem à conclusão de que o candidato representado estaria fazendo referência, anuindo ou normalizando práticas de crimes extremamente graves envolvendo crianças e adolescentes", afirmou a ministra.

A relatora também afirmou que a desinformação eleitoral não ocorre apenas quando uma informação falsa é criada, mas pode decorrer da forma como um conteúdo é apresentado.

"A desinformação eleitoral não se limita à mentira integralmente fabricada. A distorção também pode decorrer da maneira pela qual uma informação é apresentada", escreveu.

Estela Aranha ressaltou ainda que a liberdade de expressão tem proteção ampla, principalmente no debate político, que admite manifestações críticas e até contundentes contra agentes públicos e governos.

A ministra considerou também que havia risco de dano pela permanência da publicação no ar porque o conteúdo foi divulgado em uma rede social de amplo alcance e por um perfil com "expressiva capacidade de difusão".

Com esses argumentos, Estela Aranha concedeu parcialmente a liminar solicitada pela coligação.

Além da retirada da postagem e da proibição de republicação do conteúdo, o processo seguirá para manifestação da Procuradoria-Geral Eleitoral (PGE) e será submetido ao plenário do TSE.

articles.standfirst: O debate será transmitido ao vivo pela TV Globo logo após o Jornal Nacional, com início previsto para as 21h30. Estão confirmados os candidatos Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Augusto Cury (Avante) e Romeu Zema (Novo).
articles.summary: O debate será transmitido ao vivo pela TV Globo logo após o Jornal Nacional, com início previsto para as 21h30. Estão confirmados os candidatos Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiad
articles.body:
Debate de presidenciáveis na Globo acontece nesta quinta (1) — Foto: Divulgação

A TV Globo realiza nesta quinta-feira (1º) o último debate televisionado entre candidatos à Presidência da República antes do primeiro turno das Eleições 2026, marcado para domingo (4).

Mediado pelo jornalista César Tralli, o encontro será realizado direto dos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro.

Quem participará do debate presidencial da Globo?

Estão confirmados no debate da Globo os candidatos Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Augusto Cury (Avante) e Romeu Zema (Novo).

Que horas será o debate presidencial na Globo?

O debate será logo após o Jornal Nacional, com início previsto para as 21h30. Pela primeira vez, o programa ocupará a faixa da novela das 21h, "Quem Ama Cuida".

Onde e como assistir ao debate presidencial na Globo?

O encontro será transmitido ao vivo pela TV Globo direto dos Estúdios Globo, no Rio de Janeiro, e também poderá ser visto simultaneamente no g1 e na GloboNews.

O programa terá quatro blocos de perguntas e respostas, além das considerações finais. Dois blocos são de temas determinados e dois, de tema livre.

A dinâmica dos candidatos acontece ao redor de um mapa do Brasil posicionado no centro do cenário.

Por meio do mapa, o debate abordará as regiões do Brasil e temas específicos como a preservação da Amazônia; segurança nas fronteiras e combate ao crime organizado; e desafios para melhorar a infraestrutura para as exportações brasileiras.

Além disso, os candidatos poderão escolher entre temas predefinidos no telão para fazer as suas perguntas.

O candidato que faz a pergunta terá dois minutos para dividir entre a formulação da questão e a réplica. O candidato que responde terá três minutos para dividir entre resposta e tréplica.

A assessoria do presidente Lula, candidato à reeleição pelo PT, informou à Globo nesta quarta-feira (30) que e le não participará do debate que será realizado pela emissora, nesta quinta-feira (1º) à noite .

articles.title: Mendonça confirma em voto decisão que tirou do ar posts sobre Nossa Senhora Aparecida | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministros analisam decisão de Mendonça que removeu as publicações que associavam Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) a uma suposta iniciativa para retirar de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil.
articles.summary: Ministros analisam decisão de Mendonça que removeu as publicações que associavam Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) a uma suposta iniciativa para retirar de Nossa Senhora Aparecida o título de padroeira do Brasil.
articles.body:
O ministro André Mendonça , do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), se manifestou para confirmar as próprias decisões que determinaram a retirada do ar de publicações que ligavam o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) a um suposto movimento de retirada de Nossa Senhora Aparecida do posto de padroeira do Brasil.

Mendonça, autor da decisão, foi o primeiro a votar. Ele incluiu o voto nos sistemas da Justiça Eleitoral antes do horário marcado para o julgamento, às 10h . A análise vai até as 23h59 desta quarta.

Em sua manifestação, o ministro afirmou que as decisões dele não restringem a liberdade religiosa, foram determinadas em caráter excepcional e "não constituem censura prévia" (veja mais sobre o voto abaixo).

O TSE é composto por sete integrantes: três do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), dois do Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ) e dois advogados indicados pelo Supremo.

Ministro André Mendonça. — Foto: Luiz Roberto/TSE

O ministro votou para referendar as duas determinações dele sobre o tema.

➡️ Disse que a primeira decisão foi tomada porque a Justiça identificou um conjunto de informações específicas que poderiam ser verificadas e que, em uma análise inicial, foram consideradas falsas.

➡️ A decisão seguinte, na explicação dele, teve o objetivo de fazer cumprir a medida diante da ampla divulgação desse conteúdo, com base nas regras eleitorais e em decisões já tomadas pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal.

Afirmou também que seguiu o entendimento do STF sobre o Marco Civil da Internet, que ampliou a responsabilidade das plataformas pelo conteúdo dos usuários.

"A regulamentação eleitoral passou a expressamente prever o dever de os provedores promoverem a imediata remoção de conteúdos de publicações que reproduzam, no todo ou em parte, conteúdo idêntico ou substancialmente equivalente àquele objeto de fake news que já tenha sido objeto de ordem de indisponibilização pela Justiça Eleitoral, independentemente de nova ordem judicial específica", destacou no voto.

Mendonça diz que a decisão não restringe a liberdade religiosa e que continuam permitidas manifestações de fé, a defesa de Nossa Senhora Aparecida como Padroeira do Brasil, assim como críticas a uma eventual mudança dessa condição e debates sobre religião e política.

Mas a "medida alcança exclusivamente a atribuição ao candidato ou à sua família", sem evidências que a sustentem.

Na segunda-feira (28), o ministro Luiz Fux, do STF, suspendeu a decisão do ministro Flávio Dino que havia derrubado a ordem do ministro Mendonça.

Com a decisão, Fux restabeleceu, até a análise pelo plenário do STF, a determinação de Mendonça para retirar do ar as postagens, que incluíam uma publicação do humorista Antonio Tabet.

A decisão de Dino, tomada no domingo (27), havia permitido o restabelecimento do post de Tabet e de outras publicações removidas pelo mesmo fundamento.

Dino argumentou que a postagem não citava nominalmente Flávio Bolsonaro e que a medida era necessária para proteger a liberdade de expressão.

Fux, que atendeu a um pedido da defesa do candidato, defendeu que o tema fosse examinado pelo colegiado diante dos impactos sobre a Justiça Eleitoral e sobre a disputa presidencial em curso.

Após Flávio Bolsonaro recorrer da derrubada da decisão de Mendonça, Dino já havia enviado a decisão dele para aprovação no plenário.

O presidente do STF, ministro Edson Fachin , chegou a sinalizar que pautaria o assunto nesta quarta-feira (30), o que não chegou a ser confirmado.

Uma decisão colegiada na Justiça Eleitoral se sobrepõe e derruba as liminares no STF.

articles.title: Vereador que tentou subornar policial após acidente é solto da prisão | G1
articles.standfirst: Morinigo, de Ponta Porã, deixou o Presídio Militar nesta terça-feira (30) e terá de usar tornozeleira eletrônica; adolescente de 17 anos ficou gravemente ferido no acidente.
articles.summary: Morinigo, de Ponta Porã, deixou o Presídio Militar nesta terça-feira (30) e terá de usar tornozeleira eletrônica; adolescente de 17 anos ficou gravemente ferido no acidente.
articles.body:
Vereador foi preso em flagrante nesta sexta-feira (18) — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Após 11 dias preso por se envolver em um acidente, fugir do local e tentar subornar um policial civil, o vereador Morinigo, de Ponta Porã , foi solto nesta terça-feira (30) com tornozeleira eletrônica. O pedido da defesa para que o político responda ao processo em liberdade foi aceito pela Justiça de Naviraí.

O acidente ocorreu no dia 18 de setembro e deixou um adolescente de 17 anos gravemente ferido.

Morinigo deixou o Presídio Militar, em Campo Grande, no fim da tarde desta terça-feira 29). Na decisão, o juiz Fernando Moreira Freitas da Silva determinou uma série de medidas cautelares, entre elas a proibição de sair de casa após as 22h e de manter contato com a vítima e testemunhas.

O monitoramento eletrônico terá prazo inicial de 180 dias e poderá ser renovado mediante decisão fundamentada da Justiça. O descumprimento das medidas impostas poderá resultar na decretação de nova prisão.

Segundo o juiz, a manutenção da prisão preventiva poderia violar prazos legais, considerando a existência de diligências policiais ainda pendentes no caso.

Segundo os autos, Dionaldo dirigia uma Toyota Hilux quando passou em alta velocidade por uma lombada e bateu na lateral de uma Volkswagen Saveiro.

O adolescente que dirigia a Saveiro ficou desacordado e foi levado ao Hospital Regional. Conforme a decisão judicial, ele sofreu ferimentos graves.

Conforme o registro oficial, após a batida, Dionaldo fugiu sem prestar socorro. Um escrivão da Polícia Civil que presenciou o acidente seguiu a caminhonete por cerca de dois quilômetros e conseguiu abordá-lo.

Durante a abordagem, o vereador se identificou como bombeiro e agente político. Segundo o relato do policial, Dionaldo perguntou se havia uma forma de “resolver ali” a situação sem envolver os órgãos policiais. A fala foi interpretada como uma tentativa de suborno.

A Justiça também considerou que a conduta pode indicar, em tese, uma tentativa de interferir na atuação dos agentes públicos.

Ainda segundo os autos, Dionaldo teria xingado e ameaçado o escrivão, dizendo que iria “pegá-lo depois”.

Dionaldo se recusou a fazer o teste do bafômetro. Policiais registraram hálito etílico, desordem nas vestes, agressividade e exaltação. Latas de cerveja também foram encontradas na caminhonete.

Ele foi preso em flagrante e indiciado por crimes que incluem lesão corporal no trânsito, corrupção ativa, desacato e ameaça. O processo também aponta a fuga do local do acidente.

O Ministério Público de Mato Grosso do Sul (MPMS) pediu a conversão do flagrante em prisão preventiva. A Justiça aceitou o pedido e entendeu que medidas mais brandas não seriam suficientes diante das circunstâncias do caso.

Na audiência de custódia deste domingo, Dionaldo relatou ter sofrido violência durante a prisão. O juiz determinou que o caso seja encaminhado ao Grupo de Atuação Especial de Controle Externo da Atividade Policial (Gacep) para apuração.

A Justiça também suspendeu o porte de arma do vereador e manteve apreendida uma pistola Sig Sauer 9 mm. O Comando-Geral do Corpo de Bombeiros foi comunicado para adoção de medidas administrativas.

Confira os posicionamentos do partido e da defesa do parlamentar, divulgados diante da repercussão do caso.

"A defesa entende que o flagrante está exacerbado, porque não existe prova de ter ingerido bebida alcoólica, não existe prova de ter tentado subornar. O que houve foi uma discussão com o policial civil quando da tentativa da prisão. A defesa requereu a liberdade, mas o juiz entendeu que não era o momento oportuno e manteve a prisão preventiva. Na segunda-feira, a defesa vai buscar, junto ao juízo competente, a liberdade provisória, monitorada ou não, ou qualquer outra medida cautelar menos drástica que a prisão. A defesa entende que é uma barbárie a manutenção da prisão e que os requisitos estão mais do que claros para que ele possa responder em liberdade. Marcos Ivan, advogado de Dionaldo Morinigo"

"A respeito das informações veiculadas recentemente envolvendo o vereador Subtenente Morinigo, de Ponta Porã, o Partido Democrático Trabalhista (PDT) lamenta profundamente o ocorrido. O PDT reitera seu compromisso com a transparência e o respeito ao devido processo legal, e informa que acompanhará o desdobramento da Justiça e a apuração dos fatos pelas autoridades competentes. Partido Democrático Trabalhista (PDT)"

articles.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: Institutos acionam TSE contra novas regras | G1
articles.standfirst: Associação Brasileira de Empresas de Pesquisa (Abep) entrou com um mandado de segurança para questionar a obrigatoriedade de maior detalhamento no Sistema de Registro de Pesquisas Eleitorais em meio ao período eleitoral; relatoria ficou com a ministra Estela Aranha.
articles.summary: A Abep questiona no TSE a obrigatoriedade de novos detalhes no registro de pesquisas eleitorais, pedindo que as mudanças sejam facultativas nestas eleições.
articles.body:
Fachada do prédio do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) — Foto: Luiz Roberto/Secom/tse

A Associação Brasileira de Empresas de Pesquisa (Abep) entrou com um mandado de segurança no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) na noite de terça-feira (29) para questionar as mudanças anunciadas pela corte para o registro de pesquisas eleitorais no Sistema de Registro de Pesquisas Eleitorais (PesqEle) , sistema público de consulta a levantamentos de intenção de voto. A relatoria do caso, definida por sorteio, ficou com a ministra Estela Aranha.

🔍 O mandado de segurança é uma ação usada para contestar ato ilegal ou abusivo de autoridade pública que viole um direito que possa ser comprovado de imediato, só com documentos. Previsto no artigo 5º da Constituição e na Lei 12.016/2009, deve ser apresentado em até 120 dias após a ciência do ato. No caso do processo no TSE, o caso está classificado como um mandado de segurança "cível" para indicar que o tema em questão não é penal.

Em ofício assinado em 17 de setembro, o presidente do TSE, ministro Nunes Marques, passou a exigir mais detalhes sobre a coleta de dados, a metodologia e os questionários a partir de 5 de outubro, um dia depois do primeiro turno. O ofício foi enviado aos representantes legais das empresas que realizam pesquisas eleitorais.

Em nota divulgada na segunda-feira (28), a ABEP já havia criticado a adoção das novas exigências em meio ao processo eleitoral deste ano. A entidade argumentou que a implementação das mudanças deveria ocorrer somente depois de um debate técnico mais amplo com participação efetiva do setor e em “período adequado de transição”.

No documento enviado ao TSE, a entidade fez um pedido de liminar (decisão provisória) para que o preenchimento dos novos campos de informação no sistema sejam facultativos durante as eleições deste ano. Também solicita que o não preenchimento, informações incompletas ou eventuais divergências metodológicas não impeçam o registro e a divulgação de pesquisas nem produzam efeitos jurídicos que não estejam previstos na regulamentação vigente. Como alternativa, a ABEP sugere que o tribunal tenha um regime de transição para a adoção das novas exigências.

"A associação considera que o sistema eletrônico pode organizar e detalhar informações já previstas pela legislação, mas não deveria criar novas obrigações ou consequências jurídicas para o registro das pesquisas sem que essas mudanças sejam incorporadas às normas eleitorais", afirma a associação em nova nota à imprensa. "Na ação, a ABEP não questiona a ampliação da transparência das pesquisas nem a competência do TSE para aperfeiçoar o PesqEle. A discussão se concentra na forma como as novas exigências serão implementadas."

A Abep reúne empresas de pesquisas de mercado, opinião e mídia e atua na promoção de padrões de qualidade e boas práticas no setor. A entidade representa ao menos 104 empresas do setor.

Quais são as mudanças estabelecidas pelo TSE?

Algumas das novas exigências na hora do registro incluem:

descrição da amostra da pesquisa, descrevendo a população que foi entrevistada, o nível de confiança e margem de erro máxima;

detalhamento da metodologia de campo, com a base utilizada para acessar o eleitorado e a indicação o uso de mídias durante a entrevista;

exigência sobre a estrutura do questionário, com informações sobre a ordem das perguntas que foi apresentada aos entrevistados.

Além disso, para depois da divulgação das pesquisas, as empresas devem:

registrar o dia e a hora do início e do fim da realização dos questionários;

apresentar a amostra real e o descarte, mostrando o tamanho efetivo da amostra e se houve alguma recusa, perda ou substituição de entrevistados;

demonstrar o modo de coleta das respostas, incluindo a plataforma utilizada, metodologia de ponderação e medidas de precisão estatística;

trazer o cálculo da taxa de resposta e identificar eventuais limitações metodológicas em um relatório próprio.

O recurso contra o anúncio do presidente do TSE acontece dois meses depois que o ministro propôs criar um selo para reconhecer os institutos cujas pesquisas mais se aproximassem dos resultados oficiais das urnas . A proposta foi apresentada pelo presidente durante reunião com representantes do setor, sem aviso prévio. Ministros do TSE ouvidos pelo g1 também disseram que foram pegos de surpresa a respeito do tema da reunião. Eles descreveram a proposta como "constrangedora".

Depois do encontro, a entidade publicou uma nota na qual afirmou que a iniciativa parte de uma compreensão equivocada sobre a finalidade das pesquisas eleitorais. Segundo a associação, os levantamentos medem a intenção de voto no momento em que são realizados e não representam previsões ou promessas de resultado. “ Exigir que uma pesquisa ‘acerte’ o resultado é confundir ciência com bola de cristal”, afirmou a ABEP. Em minoria, Nunes Marques recuou a respeito da ideia de implementar o selo de acurácia.

articles.title: Em meio à crise no STF, Gilmar critica vazamentos em fala no aniversário de um ano da presidência de Fachin | G1

articles.summary: Gilmar disse que Fachin "tem mantido o tom sóbrio, a palavra medida e o comprometimento integral com a manutenção da constância, da tranquilidade e do ethos decisórios do Tribunal" em um "ambiente de temperatura elevada".
articles.body:
Em meio a crise institucional instalada no Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), o ministro Gilmar Mendes afirmou nesta quarta-feira(30) criticou vazamentos seletivos e uso político eleitoral de investigações.

A fala ocorreu durante uma homenagem ao aniversário de um ano da presidência do ministro Edson Fachin no STF. Tradicionalmente, o presidente e o decano, ministro que ocupa há mais tempo o cargo, fazem um discurso. Gilmar Mendes é o decano e pediu a palavra no início da sessão.

"Naquela quadra só que não houve notícias de vazamentos seletivos em nossos gabinetes. Apesar da sensibilidade dos documentos que estavam sob nossa responsabilidade. Tampouco qualquer ato que pudesse indicar uso político eleitoral das investigações", disse Gilmar ao relembrar a atuação dele e de Fachin na Operação Lava Jato.

Edson Fachin foi o relator das investigações da operação da Polícia Federal (PF) no STF, após a morte do ministro Teori Zavascki. Gilmar classificou a condução do processo por Fachin como equilibrada, sem espetáculo e sem interesses políticos. E citou discordâncias com o colega.

"Naqueles casos, divergimos com frequência, como todos sabem, sobre questões centrais da operação, como é natural em um colegiado. Nossos votos apontaram muitas vezes em sentidos opostos. a partir de compreensões distintas sobre o processo penal. Essa divergência, porém, jamais alcançou aquilo que nos unia – a convicção de que o juiz não é parte nem instrumento de causa alguma", afirmou Gilmar.

Gilmar disse que Fachin "tem mantido o tom sóbrio, a palavra medida e o comprometimento integral com a manutenção da constância, da tranquilidade e do ethos decisórios do Tribunal" em um "ambiente de temperatura elevada".

O decano do STF também destacou julgamentos na gestão de Fachin como:

as restrições para o pagamento de penduricalhos de juízes e integrantes do Ministério Público;

aquisição de imóveis rurais por empresas brasileiras controladas por capital estrangeiro;

validade da lei que alterou os limites do Parque Nacional do Jamanxim, no Pará, para permitir a passagem da ferrovia destinada a ligar a produção do Centro-Oeste aos portos do Arco Norte; e

validade da lei que trata da igualdade salarial e de critérios remuneratórios entre mulheres e homens.

Montagem com fotos dos ministros Gilmar Mendes e Edson Fachin, do STF — Foto: Carlos Moura/SCO/STF

Criticado pela demora em responder à crise instalada no STF, Fachin recebeu um elogio do procurador Geral da República (PGR), Paulo Gonet, que afirmou que Fachin sabe quando e como agir.

“Vossa Excelência é sobretudo um homem do diálogo, do diálogo sereno, do diálogo franco, afável, aberto e eficaz. Mas Vossa Excelência também sabe como e quando agir”, disse o procurador-geral.

“Essas qualidades demonstradas por Vossa Excelência nesse primeiro ano do biênio da sua presidência nos dá segurança e tranquilidade quanto à última etapa da do seu biênio à frente do Tribunal”, complementou o PGR.

articles.title: Lula diz que Flávio Bolsonaro foi eleito pelo crime organizado | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente deu a declaração durante entrevista com influenciadores nesta quarta-feira (30). Ele questionou o crescimento do conservadorismo entre pessoas com maior grau de escolaridade.
articles.summary: Em entrevista, Lula criticou a trajetória de Flávio Bolsonaro, citou supostas ligações com milícias e questionou o avanço do conservadorismo entre eleitores com maior grau de escolaridade.
articles.body:
Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert e Vittor Sales

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) criticou, nesta quarta-feira (30), o adversário nas urnas Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). O petista disse que o candidato à Presidência pelo PL não tem biografia, e foi eleito a cargos públicos "pelo crime organizado".

Lula deu a declaração durante entrevista a influenciadores, como parte da agenda de campanha.

Ele afirmou que há um crescimento do nível de conservadorismo de acordo com o grau de escolaridade dos brasileiros.

"Quanto mais as pessoas são graduadas, mais elas são conservadoras. Você não fica com pena disso? Eu quando vejo um cara com diploma, um economista, votar no Bolsonaro eu fico pensando o que é que esse cara espera da vida? O que esse cara aprendeu de política na vida?", questionou.

"Vamos pegar esse Flávio, qual é o compromisso com qualquer seriedade que esse cara tem? Nenhuma, ele não tem biografia. Ele nunca trabalhou na vida. Ele foi eleito vereador com 21 anos de idade já apoiado pelo crime organizado no Rio de Janeiro, pelos milicianos, e nunca mais parou", disse.

"Eu queria que alguém me dissesse o que esse cara tem pra oferecer. Nada, não tem conteúdo", prosseguiu.

🔎As suspeitas de elo entre Flávio e milicianos surgiram na época que ele era deputado estadual no Rio de Janeiro e contratou em seu gabinete na Alerj parentes do miliciano Adriano da Nóbrega, apontado como chefe do "Escritório do Crime". Além disso, quando era deputado estadual, Flávio concedeu honrarias a policiais suspeitos de envolvimento com milícias.

🔎O candidato do PL nega ligação com milicianos e diz que as condecorações dadas valorizavam policiais até então considerados "fichas-limpas".

A emenda foi negociada em 2023 entre Peixe e Maria de Fátima Bezerra Castro, secretária parlamentar no gabinete de Flávio no Senado. Marielle e seu motorista Anderson Gomes foram mortos em 2018.

A Polícia Federal tem indícios de que o dinheiro da emenda foi desviado. As conversas sobre a emenda foram noticiadas primeiramente pelo jornal "O Estado de S. Paulo" e pela revista "Piauí". Em maio, o jornal "O Globo" já havia revelado a existência da investigação.

A PF encontrou mensagens de WhatsApp trocadas entre Peixe e Maria de Fátima no celular do miliciano, apreendido quando ele passou a ser investigado pela morte de Marielle, em 2024. O g1 obteve os prints das conversas (veja aqui).

articles.title: Democrats want a blue wave. New Hampshire is Exhibit A for why that may not happen
articles.summary: Five weeks before Election Day, Democratic enthusiasm is reaching a fever pitch.  With Republicans struggling to overcome President Donald Trump's low standi...
articles.body:
HUDSON, N.H. (AP) — Five weeks before Election Day , Democratic enthusiasm is reaching a fever pitch.

With Republicans struggling to overcome President Donald Trump's low standing, Democrats are on the offensive in Republican strongholds like Texas and Florida, and even eyeing contests in deeper-red Kansas and Mississippi. Many Democratic leaders predict that the House majority is all but theirs, and that the Senate majority, almost unthinkable a year ago, is nearly in their grasp as well.

In the midst of such confidence, however, Democrats are ignoring glaring vulnerabilities that threaten to undermine the unstoppable blue wave they say is coming.

Look no further than swing-state New Hampshire, where Democratic leaders are sounding the alarm about political challenges that could jeopardize Rep. Chris Pappas' campaign for an open Senate seat and undermine the party's ability to win races around the country.

Democrats point to Republicans' overwhelming financial advantage that is allowing them to dominate the airwaves in the closing days of the campaign. At the same time, the Democrats' brand remains deeply unpopular, and they have virtually no margin for error in midterm races that are playing out largely in Republican-leaning states.

New Hampshire Democratic Chairman Ray Buckley says that national Democratic leaders "have consistently been overly optimistic" as they look to expand the midterm map. He's particularly worried about his state's Senate contest, where Republicans are investing far more resources than Democrats.

"There is reason for concern," Buckley said. "We don't want to let this one slip away because they were sending resources to some other unicorns — some other state that's just not possible."

Despite such warnings, there is little sign of concern among senior Democratic officials, who point to Trump's poor standing with voters who are frustrated by the war with Iran and surging costs with Republicans in control of Washington.

"It's nothing we're doing. We're winning because they're losing," said Democratic pollster John Anzalone. "And they're losing dramatically with every action the president has taken."

There is almost no state where Democrats cannot compete in November, he said: "America is the battleground state."

Democrats are short on cash and goodwill

For all the Democrats' confidence, the party's brand remains deeply unpopular and fundraising is lagging.

More than half of voters, 55%, have a "strongly" or "somewhat" unfavorable view of the Democrats, according to a Fox News poll from September. A similar share, 58%, say the same about the Republican Party, while about 6 in 10 voters have a negative view of Trump (62%).

At the same time, about half of registered voters say the Democratic Party is "too far to the left," according to a recent New York Times/Siena poll.

As the election approaches, few Democratic leaders acknowledge there is a problem.

In an interview, Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., pointed the finger at Republicans when asked about issues with the Democratic brand.

"We've made a much better case than them, and that's why it looks like we're going to win a bunch of House seats and probably win back the Senate," Kelly said. "Right now, I think the Republican brand is the one that's damaged."

And yet Democrats are struggling to keep up with Republican fundraising.

Flush with campaign cash, Republicans are dominating the airwaves over the final weeks of the campaign. There isn't a single state that features a top-tier Senate contest in which Democrats are spending more than Republicans.

Nationwide, Republicans are spending $1.63 billion on campaign advertising between Sept. 1 and Election Day compared to $1.19 billion for Democrats, according to data compiled by AdImpact as of Monday. The Republican advantage, nearly 40% nationwide, is actually larger in some key states.

In Texas, for example, which features competitive races for the Senate, House and governor, Republicans are spending $262.4 million statewide between Sept. 1 and Election Day compared to $76.9 million for Democrats, AdImpact found. In Ohio, which also hosts pivotal elections for Senate and governor, Republicans are outspending Democrats $258.8 million to $160.4 million. And in Florida, which features competitive races for governor and the House, Republicans are spending $99.3 million against the Democrats' $47.9 million.

The Republican advantage isn't as egregious in New Hampshire as some other states, but it is significant. AdImpact finds that Republicans are outspending Democrats in New Hampshire $41.2 million to $35.4 million statewide.

Pappas, the Democrat in the New Hampshire Senate race, acknowledged the Republican spending advantage and warned that his state must remain a priority for his national party.

"The majority won't be flipped if we don't hold this seat in New Hampshire, so it's really critical to the overall map," he said during a campaign stop.

Pappas met on Tuesday with small business owners, including Amber Morgan, who owns Fortin Gage Flowers in Nashua. She said the uncertainty created by the Trump administration's tariffs have been hard for her business.

But Morgan, a Democrat, is not surprised that New Hampshire's Senate race is close, given that Republicans are running the well-known former Sen. John E. Sununu. She said the Democratic Party has its faults as well.

"I think that the message for so long has just been, 'We're not Trump,' and we've had a bit of an identity crisis in terms of what we actually stand for," Morgan said.

Nationwide, the NYT/Siena poll found that about 6 in 10 registered voters who identify as Democrats say their party is divided, while only about 4 in 10 Republicans (37%) say the same about the GOP. Roughly 6 in 10 Republicans (61%) describe their party as united, compared to about 4 in 10 Democrats (40%).

But money remains the Democrats' dominant concern as the Republican spending advantage grows.

Steve Marchand, a Democratic consultant and former New Hampshire gubernatorial candidate, said Sununu has benefited from national money that got redirected from other states that are no longer seen as top targets, while Democrats were slower to invest.

"Democrats, including Pappas, became increasingly frustrated that national Democrats treated it like a fait accompli, like 'you guys have it up there, we're going to other states,'" Marchand said. "And a lot of us Democrats were saying, 'Hey, Sununu is going to be formidable, and New Hampshire is not a right-down-the-ticket kind of state.'"

Fred Osterholtz, a sales engineer at one of the businesses Pappas visited, said he's worried about the huge amounts of money being poured into the race on Sununu's behalf as well. But he was impressed with Pappas' focus.

"I think he's starting to find some of the messages that will resonate," Osterholtz said. "I didn't feel that way six months ago, but with the world stage the way it is — the costs, the inflation — they're latching onto the right things I think."

Peoples reported from New York and Sloan reported from Washington. Associated Press writer Linley Sanders in Washington contributed.

articles.title: Elon Musk says AI promises wealth and great healthcare for all, but 'jobs are going to change'
articles.summary: Elon Musk said AI would change how jobs look in future, but this is nothing new, and isn't necessarily a bad thing.
articles.body:
Elon Musk says AI may herald an "age of abundance" where everyone's rich and has stellar healthcare.

The Tesla and SpaceXAI CEO said that jobs will change, but that's happened throughout history.

Musk spoke at the White House after joining other tech leaders in pledging to build AI responsibly.

Elon Musk expects AI to create a world where everyone has lots of cash and top-notch healthcare, but says jobs will look different from today.

"I think by far the most likely outcome is an age of abundance where we don't have just universal basic income, we have universal high income," the Tesla and SpaceXAI CEO told reporters following a meeting of tech leaders at the White House on Tuesday.

"When you have robots, and you have superintelligence, it means that everyone in the world can have better medical care than anyone here, including me," Musk continued, describing that possibility as "wonderful."

Asked about AI potentially destroying jobs , the world's richest man replied that "jobs are going to change," but that's nothing new. He quipped that "being a computer used to be a job," but now digital computers crunch the numbers, and he doubts "anyone is pining to go back and do calculations all day."

Musk also noted that AI hasn't yet caused unemployment to spike , and instead, there's "tremendous demand for people." He added that he anticipates an "incredibly beneficial" outcome for humanity from AI, a "future you would want."

The serial entrepreneur joined Nvidia's Jensen Huang, Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Alphabet's Sundar Pichai, OpenAI's Greg Brockman, and Anthropic's Dario Amodei in signing a "Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities."

Following a resurgence of fears of an AI apocalypse , the tech bosses behind AI chatbots, including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok, agreed to develop the tech safely and responsibly.

They pledged to impose "robust internal controls" overseen by a dedicated internal team, an independent external auditor or evaluator, and an independent board committee.

Musk, when he's not standing next to Trump, has not always struck a massively upbeat tone about AI's potential impacts. In previous interviews, he's said the risk of AI and robots going catastrophically wrong is " not zero ," and he foresees a "bumpy" transition to a bright future.

"Universal HIGH INCOME via checks issued by the Federal government is the best way to deal with unemployment caused by AI," he posted on X in April.

He's publicly imagined a utopia where everyone can have "all the stuff they want," as new technologies will drive production costs so low that there will be virtually unlimited goods and services. But he's also flagged the risk that if people's jobs don't matter, they could lose their sense of purpose in life.

Musk has also said that if he's right about what the future holds, people shouldn't worry about saving for retirement in 10 or 20 years, as their nest eggs will be " irrelevant ."

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.) on Tuesday blasted Sen. Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.) after he and his staff appeared to confuse one basketball team for another when questioning former special counsel Jack Smith about his attendance at a game.

Schmitt earlier Tuesday asked Smith if he attended a February 2024 NBA game in Atlanta between the Hawks and the Golden State Warriors. The inquiry and subsequent exchange drew in other senators and sparked confusion after he appeared to mistake the Iowa Hawkeyes for the Atlanta Hawks.

"Look, nobody ever heard of Sen. Schmitt before, and nobody's going to ever hear of him again," Raskin, the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, told CNN's Erin Burnett. "He's basically disgraced himself and identified himself with this ridiculous little stunt where he thought he was going to perform some major service to Donald Trump."

Raskin added that Schmitt's questioning was "all about being the most obsequious sycophant you can be, and he proved that he was."

"And he doesn't even understand how much that he's utterly humiliated himself in the eyes of the country," he added.

Burnett asked if Schmitt will apologize to Smith for the mix-up, to which Raskin answered, "Well, not from the looks of it." Smith at first denied attending the game before Schmitt's staff displayed a poster of texts of the ex-federal prosecutor's staff discussing seat numbers, and Schmitt said "for context" the date of the game was just after Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis (D) acknowledged a romance with a colleague, an incident that shook up the 2020 election interference case in Georgia against President Trump. Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) also weighed in during the hearing, saying, "It looked like he had text messages suggesting that Jack Smith was at some sporting event he wasn't at, and he hoped to catch Jack Smith in some false statement."

"It turns out the only thing false was the presentation," he added.

articles.title: Democrats split on AOC as some battleground candidates distance themselves from 'Squad' lawmaker
articles.summary: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez rallied with Bernie Sanders for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, but some 2026 midterm candidates are distancing themselves.
articles.body: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., is fast becoming a central figurehead in the 2026 midterm election cycle, and a polarizing one at that. Some moderate candidates are shunning the progressive rising star's endorsement, Axios reported this week, while others in tight races are welcoming her with open arms. Several Democratic strategists who spoke with Fox News Digital said they were not shocked that some on the left are keeping her at arm's length. "It wasn't especially surprising, like, her numbers with independent voters aren't always great, and it's very circumstantial depending upon where you would want to deploy somebody with that type of background and somebody who, you know, a lot of Americans have an impression of already — sometimes positive, sometimes negative," Mike Nellis, a former political advisor for former Vice President Kamala Harris, told Fox News Digital. "I always just encourage people, like, you do what you gotta do, cause it's hard to play coalition politics." DEMOCRAT CHALLENGING MIKE LAWLER WON'T COMMIT ON CAMPAIGNING WITH AOC, MAMDANI OR REJECTING DSA And there are at least two candidates who appear to think the original "Squad" member is more of a liability. HASAN PIKER SAYS HE’D ‘ABSOLUTELY’ CAMPAIGN FOR AOC IN 2028 AS EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF Cait Conley, who is running to unseat Rep. Mike Lawler, R-N.Y., in a district near Ocasio-Cortez's, told CNN's "State of the Union," "I'm good" when asked if she would campaign with Democratic socialists like her or New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Conley's campaign did not return a request for comment by Fox News Digital by publication time. And Sam Forstag in Montana reportedly removed all mention of Ocasio-Cortez's endorsement from his campaign website. He told Axios, "I don't intend to be having a lot of folks from out of state campaigning with me over these next 40 days." Forstag's campaign did not return multiple emailed requests for comment by Fox News Digital. JAMES CARVILLE PREDICTS 2028 DEMOCRATIC PRIMARY WILL TEST TRUE STRENGTH OF PARTY'S SOCIALIST WING "In the final days leading up to an election, you want to make your message specific and local and repeatable and national celebrities just don’t help with that," a veteran Democratic strategist who works on House and Senate campaigns told Fox News Digital. The strategist, who asked to remain anonymous to speak more freely, said "AOC is more of a celebrity" than most of the other potential 2028 Democratic presidential contenders. "I think AOC is one of the few Democrats who has transcended to just culture generally, which makes her visits heavier in the discourse." And that celebrity status is being used in other key races. Ocasio-Cortez joined forces with fellow progressive champion Sen. Bernie Sanders to headline a trio of rallies for left-wing candidate Abdul El-Sayed in July, a couple of weeks before the Democratic Senate primary in the key battleground state of Michigan. El-Sayed ended up narrowly edging more moderate Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., in a nomination battle that highlighted the ongoing battle between the left and the center for the ideological future of the Democratic Party. While Ocasio-Cortez has yet to return to Michigan since the early August primary, El-Sayed’s campaign says they’d welcome her return to the campaign trail. "There are a lot of Michiganders who can't wait to have AOC back in town," El-Sayed campaign communications director Roxie Richner told Fox News Digital. AOC BACKS FLORIDA DEM ANGIE NIXON FOR US SENATE: 'I’M PROUD TO ENDORSE HER' El-Sayed and former House Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., are facing off in the race to succeed Sen. Gary Peters, D-Mich. The midterm showdown is a must-hold for the Democrats as they try to win back the Senate majority from the Republicans. Ocasio-Cortez also appeared in Florida recently alongside far-left Senate candidate Angie Nixon, who is running an underdog campaign against Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla. A Democratic victory there is a long shot, but Ocasio-Cortez's campaign trail travels come as speculation mounts about her own future political plans. The Democratic socialist is widely seen as a potential successor to Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., when he is through in the upper chamber. But there's also buzz about a potential 2028 presidential campaign — something Ocasio-Cortez has not confirmed nor denied. "I think she's a unique political talent. She's clearly got, like, a large group of people in the country who would get behind her, and those are the beginnings of what you need to build an operation to run for president. So I think she'd be stupid not to think about it," Nellis said. "At the same time, you know, do you take a 5% chance of being the Democratic nominee... or do you take like a much better than 50-50 chance of being the next United States senator from New York? If it were me advising her, I'd probably tell her to run for Senate." articles.title: Why is Hegseth cutting 20 percent of US general and admiral positions?
articles.summary: The overhaul could reshape the US military as Hegseth faces scrutiny over senior officers’ removal.
articles.body:
United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth plans to cut the number of positions in the US military reserved for generals and admirals by 20 percent, raising concerns about political interference in the military’s leadership amid strained relations with senior Pentagon officials .

An announcement is expected on Wednesday when Hegseth gives his “State of the Force” address to junior officers and enlisted personnel at Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia.

The Pentagon has presented previous cuts as a way to reduce bureaucracy. But analysts say Hegseth’s latest changes may be aimed at sidelining experienced commanders, discouraging dissent and appointing more officers loyal to President Donald Trump to the ranks.

So is the US military too top-heavy, and what could the cuts mean? Here’s what we know.

Citing Pentagon officials, The Associated Press news agency has reported that Hegseth will double the 10 percent reduction in top-ranking personnel ordered last year, bringing the total decrease to 20 percent by January 1, 2027. The plan affects roughly 800 general and admiral positions across the one- to four-star ranks.

Congress sets statutory limits on the number of generals and admirals. A Congressional Research Service report recorded 848 active-duty generals and admirals in September 2025, below the authorised maximum of 857.

Cutting positions does not necessarily mean immediately dismissing everyone occupying them. An official told the Reuters news agency that some roles would be eliminated, while others would be assigned to lower-ranking officers.

Why are top-ranking military positions being removed?

The argument for reducing senior ranks predates Hegseth’s tenure, with supporters saying fewer layers of command would reduce administrative work and give officers closer to operations greater authority.

Walter Ladwig, a political scientist specialising in US foreign policy at King’s College London, said there is a credible case for reform. “Since the end of the Cold War, the overall size of the force has declined significantly, but we haven’t seen a corresponding reduction in the number of flag officers,” he told Al Jazeera.

“At the same time, we’ve seen headquarters and staffs proliferate.”

Trump and Hegseth have already fired or pushed into retirement more than two dozen military leaders since Trump took office in January 2025.

Those removed include General Randy George , the US Army’s top uniformed officer, in April, and Admiral Lisa Franchetti, the chief of naval operations, in February 2025. The administration also dismissed the only two women serving as four-star officers, alongside other senior female officers.

In February 2025, Trump also fired Air Force General CQ Brown as chairman of the US Joint Chiefs of Staff as part of a wider shake-up of top military leadership.

Other departures have been of civilian leaders. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned in late August after reported disagreements over Hegseth’s handling of senior military personnel.

The dismissals, alongside blocked promotions, have raised questions about how the administration selects commanders and whether professional disagreements could jeopardise careers. Robert Ralston, a lecturer in political science and international studies at the University of Birmingham in the United Kingdom, said the proposed reductions should be weighed alongside these earlier decisions.

“These cuts appear to be part of a broader, sustained effort by Hegseth to fill the ranks based on political, rather than meritocratic, considerations,” he told Al Jazeera.

“Politics is driving these decisions, in my view.”

What political fallout could there be from this?

Democratic Senator Mark Kelly of Arizona criticised Hegseth’s changes at the Pentagon. “The US military doesn’t need more testosterone; it needs better leadership at this point,” Kelly told MS NOW’s Morning Joe programme last week.

“The consequences of firing all these admirals and generals are that we’re losing a portion, a good portion, of a generation of great leadership.”

David Galbreath, professor of war and technology at the University of Bath in the UK, told Al Jazeera that resistance from Congress and military leaders could complicate the changes.

He pointed to the opposition that arose to President Jimmy Carter’s plans to withdraw US ground troops from South Korea as an example of how military and congressional pressure can constrain a president.

“I suspect that after the election, we are likely to see a much more confrontational Congress with investigations and impeachments of Hegseth,” he said.

Whether that prediction comes true will likely depend on November’s congressional elections and whether the Republican Party retains control of both chambers of Congress.

What criticisms have been made of Hegseth?

Hegseth’s tenure at the Pentagon has been marked by controversy and tensions with senior officials. In March 2025, he shared details of forthcoming strikes on Yemen in a Signal chat group which inadvertently included The Atlantic’s editor-in-chief.

A number of US media reports about the dwindling supplies of weapons in the Middle East prompted his department to investigate leaks and restrict journalists’ access earlier this year. The New York Times reported in August that about 50 Joint Staff military and civilian officials had undergone polygraph tests amid growing mistrust inside the Pentagon.

Hegseth has meanwhile made ending what he calls “woke” culture a central priority, introducing new physical fitness requirements and abolishing diversity policies.

Ralston said the combination of dismissals and blocked promotions could damage morale and the military’s future leadership. “His relationship with senior military leaders has been adversarial, his scuttling of promotions has undoubtedly damaged morale, and will have long-term consequences for leadership pipelines within the Department of Defense,” he said.

King’s College’s Ladwig also described Hegseth’s relationship with senior Pentagon leaders as unusually confrontational but cautioned against interpreting every proposed cut as a power struggle.

“When a military is under civilian control, it means that the elected government has the right to determine defence priorities and reorganise the armed forces accordingly,” he said.

But Ladwig warned that the changes could encourage officers to hold back their professional recommendations when advising senior politicians. “That might create incentives for military officers to censor themselves rather than provide candid professional military advice, particularly if being politically aligned with the administration is seen as a path to success,” he said.

“This is a very worrisome pathology, and it’s the kind of thing that produces ineffective militaries in dictatorships.”

articles.title: GOP fortress is under threat in one key red state, and these voters could decide whether it falls
articles.summary: Black and Hispanic voter turnout could decide whether James Talarico breaks a 30-year Democratic drought in the Texas Senate race this fall.
articles.body: DALLAS — A competitive Senate race is testing whether Texas is still safely red, with Black and Hispanic voters at the center of Democrat James Talarico's path to victory. Talarico is seeking to become the first Democrat in more than 30 years to win a statewide race in the Lone Star State. "I definitely do think, if there’s any time for Texas to get a Democrat elected, this is the time to strike," Mike, a military veteran from Dallas, told Fox News Digital. "I think it depends on whether the Black and Brown voters come out for Talarico." POLL: TALARICO TIES PAXTON IN TEXAS SENATE RACE, THREATENING GOP STRONGHOLD "Everyone says, ‘Hey, we are Texas and we want change here, we want change there,’" Mike added. "Well, this is an opportunity for you guys to get change. Are you going to come out and show up at the polls? He’s got all the momentum in the world. He’s got everything going for him." Mike’s comments reflect the challenge facing Talarico as he works to build support among Black and Hispanic voters and motivate them to turn out in November. Texas has more Black eligible voters than any other state, with roughly 2.7 million. That puts voters in Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth and East Texas in a potentially decisive position in any Democrat’s bid to win statewide. Former President Barack Obama’s appearance with Talarico at a May campaign stop in Austin underscored the stakes for Democrats to leverage a massive voting bloc in Texas. The party's effort to win over Black voters could help determine whether Texas remains reliably red or becomes more competitive for Democrats in future elections. TEXAS VOTERS HAVE PLENTY TO SAY ABOUT WHETHER LONE STAR STATE COULD TURN BLUE But Talarico faces an uphill battle in uniting Democrats behind his campaign after a divisive primary against Rep. Jasmine Crockett, D-Texas. Talarico defeated Crockett in the Democratic primary earlier this year, and the outgoing congresswoman has not endorsed his Senate campaign. Crockett has said she supports the Democratic ticket in Texas, but her political action committee has not endorsed Talarico or campaigned for him. Rashaun, of Forney, Texas, said the primary loss may have left some Black voters frustrated. "Everyone was behind Jasmine," Rashaun said. "So that’s what’s blocking, I’m going to say for my people, that was blocking their minds." Still, Rashaun said she plans to vote for Talarico and hopes Texas will turn blue in November. "Yes, we are voting in November and it’s going to be Talarico," she said. "We need Texas to flip. We can wish and hope and pray. But we need to get out and vote." TEXAS VOTERS HAVE PLENTY TO SAY ABOUT WHETHER LONE STAR STATE COULD TURN BLUE Mike said the election may ultimately come down to whether voters are willing to act. "Right now it is on the Texas voters to get out and support James Talarico or sit at home if you don’t want to see that change," he said. Bryant, of Coppell, Texas, likewise pointed to frustration with Gov. Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton, both Republicans, as a potential motivator for people to support Talarico's candidacy. "This is a critical election," Bryant said. "I think we all can feel it in Texas, the need to get Greg Abbott out." REPUBLICANS JUST GOT A POWERFUL NEW PLAYBOOK FOR THE BATTLE FOR CONGRESS. HERE'S WHAT'S INSIDE "It’s time for a change," he added. "Plus, on the other side, you see how bad Ken Paxton is and his track record and just some of the things that he’s done. It’s no longer working and we need to do something different." Ava, a college student from Denton, said Talarico’s outreach to younger voters has helped him connect with a generation that often feels overlooked. "I do think he’s going to pull through," she said. "He engages with the younger community, which is important because we feel like we’re not represented." She added that his social media presence has also helped younger voters connect with his campaign. She first learned about Talarico after meeting him at the Texas State Fair last year and later followed him online. "I think he’s going to flip the state." While Ava focused on Talarico’s appeal among younger voters, Kiara, of Dallas, said supporters must turn that enthusiasm into votes. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I live in Texas, and I’ve been here for a really long time, and it’s time for a change, a positive change," she said. "And I think Talarico is definitely going to bring that." "We just have to vote," Kiara added. "We can’t complain about the problems if you don’t want to vote to fix them."

articles.title: Secret phone record seizure sparks personal lawsuit from GOP senator
articles.summary: Marsha Blackburn's lawsuit targets Jack Smith personally, arguing the special counsel was never lawfully appointed and violated her constitutional rights.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: A top Republican senator whose phone toll records were secretly subpoenaed during Jack Smith's investigation of President Donald Trump sued the former special counsel in his personal capacity Wednesday, arguing he was never lawfully empowered to wield the authority behind the Arctic Frost investigation. The lawsuit, Senator Marsha Blackburn v. John L. Smith, argues the prosecutor lacked lawful authority to serve as special counsel and violated the lawmaker's rights by obtaining the records. Blackburn is asking a federal court to declare Smith's appointment unconstitutional, order the records destroyed and award $1 in nominal damages. The case therefore seeks to test not only Smith’s tactics, but the legitimacy of the authority he claims to have exercised as special counsel appointed by then-Attorney General Merrick Garland during the Biden administration. "This lawsuit is solely about holding Mr. Smith accountable and ensuring that our nation’s justice system can never again be weaponized against the American people," Blackburn, R-Tenn., told Fox News Digital. JACK SMITH HIT WITH CRIMINAL REFERRAL AS GOP MOVES TESTIMONY FIGHT TOWARD PROSECUTION "Through his Arctic Frost witch-hunt that targeted conservatives across America and even the president of the United States, Jack Smith perpetrated one of the worst abuses of government power in our nation’s history," she said. Blackburn’s suit argues that Smith lacked lawful authority to hold the office he purported to exercise, while separately seeking to impose personal liability on him for the way that purported authority was used against her. JACK SMITH THRUST BACK INTO SPOTLIGHT AT BLANCHE HEARING OVER EXPOSED SENATORS’ MESSAGES The case opens a new legal front against Smith one day after his contentious Senate Judiciary Committee testimony, during which he acknowledged approving subpoenas for members of Congress despite understanding that nondisclosure orders prevented them from challenging the seizures under the Constitution's Speech or Debate Clause. Smith is a longtime prosecutor who most recently served as special counsel overseeing the Justice Department's investigations into President Donald Trump. Earlier in his career, he prosecuted cases before the International Criminal Court and led the DOJ's Public Integrity Section, which brought bribery charges against former Virginia Republican Gov. Robert F. McDonnell in a case where the Supreme Court later unanimously vacated the conviction. Arctic Frost was the codename for the FBI investigation into Trump's handling of classified documents and alleged efforts to overturn the 2020 election before the probe was handed over to Smith by then-Attorney General Merrick Garland. Blackburn and her data were swept up in the probe after Smith's team subpoenaed toll records from her and several other Republicans—a move that sparked outrage at Tuesday's Senate Judiciary Committee hearing over whether obtaining the records without notification violated the Constitution. In May 2023, Smith’s office issued a grand-jury subpoena seeking Verizon toll records, while a separate nondisclosure order barred the company from notifying affected customers—including Blackburn—that its information had been turned over. While the records did not reveal the contents of conversations, they showed whom Blackburn communicated with, when and for how long, according to the complaint. The lawsuit alleges that Smith’s office obtained a court-approved nondisclosure order without informing the judge that the subpoena sought records belonging to a sitting U.S. senator. JACK SMITH'S TRUMP PROBE SWEPT UP FOX NEWS, OTHER MEDIA COMMUNICATIONS AS INVESTIGATION WENT BEYOND LAWMAKERS More broadly, Smith’s team issued 197 subpoenas to 34 individuals and 163 businesses seeking information involving at least 430 Republican individuals and entities, according to Senate Judiciary Committee records. Tuesday’s hearing also began with a scathing rebuke from Chairman Charles Grassley, R-Iowa, who accused Smith’s prosecutors of sweeping up communications between journalists at Fox News and other media organizations and sources connected to the first Trump administration. For his part, Smith repeatedly hit back at allegations of corrupt or partisan prosecution, saying at one point his "investigation developed proof beyond a reasonable doubt that President Trump engaged in serious crimes against our nation." Blackburn's suit is being brought by the nonpartisan New Civil Liberties Alliance (NCLA) on her behalf, and the Tennessee senator thanked the group for its partnership. JACK SMITH'S SENATE PHONE RECORDS PROBE TURNS TO VERIZON'S HANDLING OF SUBPOENAS Blackburn’s attorneys argue that Smith exercised special counsel powers without lawful constitutional or statutory authorization. Separately, the complaint names Smith in his personal capacity and seeks to hold him liable for alleged violations of Blackburn’s constitutional and civil rights arising from the subpoena and nondisclosure order. "Jack Smith was illegally named Special Counsel in November of 2022, with Attorney General Merrick Garland handing a private citizen the sweeping powers of a special counsel," NCLA said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital. "Then-President Biden did not nominate Smith, nor did the Senate confirm Smith as either Special Counsel or in any other position. And no statute authorized his appointment." "NCLA’s complaint asks the court to declare Smith’s appointment unlawful under the Constitution’s Appointments Clause and to hold Smith accountable, in his personal capacity, for his gross abuses of power." VETERAN DEM BREAKS PARTY LINE AS JACK SMITH SPYING SCANDAL GRIPS CAPITOL HILL The suit alleges the subpoena violated Blackburn’s constitutional and civil rights and that the nondisclosure order prevented her from challenging the demand under the Constitution’s Speech or Debate Clause. "This lawsuit is not only about the faux authority granted to Smith through an unconstitutional appointment. It is also about ensuring that the Department of Justice—the very body responsible for enforcing federal law on behalf of our nation—acts only within its constitutional bounds," NCLA counsel L. Margaret Harker said in a statement. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER The lawsuit seeks a declaration that Smith's appointment was unconstitutional, the return and destruction of Blackburn's phone records, and $1 in nominal damages. NCLA says the limited damages request reflects Blackburn's stated goal of obtaining judicial accountability for what the complaint alleges were constitutional violations committed while Smith exercised special counsel powers. articles.title: Explosive sleeper issue could fuel midterm shakeups, top Republican predicts: ‘You’re gonna see surprises’
articles.summary: Tom Emmer says fraud is the top issue driving Minnesota voters to the polls and predicts Republican "surprises" in several midterm elections.
articles.body: LEWISTON, MAINE - With just about a month left until the midterm elections, Rep. Tom Emmer (R-MN) told Fox News Digital that fraud is an issue motivating voters to the polls, and in Minnesota, his home state, he thinks the issue could yield some "surprises" at the ballot box. "Fraud is a lot more important to the U.S. taxpayers than being a Republican or a Democrat," Emmer said. "People want good government. They want to know that they're paying for good government, that they are not having their hard-earned taxpayer dollars being siphoned off and stolen and sent out of the country. They're also asking, why hasn't anyone called this out and held these people accountable? And I think you're going to see that at the ballot box on November 3." Emmer, the House Majority Whip, was in Maine with Republican House candidate Paul LePage, the first stop of his planned 56-district nationwide blitz across the United States, rallying voters for Republicans as the party tries to hold on their razor-thin majority in the House against daunting historical and political headwinds. Emmer’s home state of Minnesota was the epicenter of fraud’s explosion into the national conversation late last year, prompting Gov. Tim Walz to abandon his re-election bid. Emmer expressed optimism that Republicans in Minnesota will resonate with voters on fraud in a state where a Republican hasn’t won a statewide election since 2006. KLOBUCHAR'S FRAUD FIGHT CLAIM TAKES HIT AFTER GOP OPPONENT COMBS THROUGH RECEIPTS: 'WHERE WERE YOU?' "Fraud in Minnesota is the number one issue," Emmer said. "We've got a completely incompetent, I would argue corrupt in some instances, governor and an attorney general who took campaign funds from Somali fraudsters that he was actively trying to protect from getting caught in their fraud. This is a big deal for Minnesotans." Emmer said voters are looking for an "honest system that actually works for the people" and not "the criminals" and the Republican candidates for Senate, governor, attorney general and auditor in Minnesota have all made fighting fraud a central issue of their campaigns. NEW AUDIT IN WALZ'S BACKYARD EXPOSES MASSIVE FRAUD RISK TIED TO POST-GEORGE FLOYD ACTIVISM "You easily could have Michelle Tafoya being the next U.S. Senator from the state of Minnesota, a Republican, you could have Lisa Demuth as the Republican governor and already, the attorney general candidate, Ron Schutz and the state auditor candidate Scott Jensen, the polling showing that they are leading," Emmer said. "So yes, Minnesota is going to be one of those places where you see surprises. I think you're gonna see surprises in Michigan as well and other places all across the country." Emmer sat down for a roundtable discussion on fraud with LePage, Maine’s former governor running for Congress in the state’s 2nd Congressional District, where the Minnesota Republican railed against the lack of accountability for fraud in his home state. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "They need to be held accountable and that's the one thing that's missing again in Minnesota. You've got all of these fraudsters being charged and convicted, not one public official has been charged at all, and that's got to change, and I hope it changes in Maine and other places, because it's high time that people be held accountable for ripping off the generous American people," Emmer told the panel. The Trump administration has made combating fraud a central focus this year, creating a Justice Department Fraud Division and a White House task force led by Vice President JD Vance. The White House says the task force has uncovered roughly $245.7 billion in fraud since its creation, while also stopping an additional $62.9 billion annually and enforcing $59.1 billion through criminal charges, settlements and penalties.

articles.title: Trump DOJ investigating Dem group in Texas after viral undercover video sparks massive uproar
articles.summary: A viral undercover video showing a Texas Majority PAC employee describing a "Paid Relational Program" has now triggered a DOJ investigation.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: A Texas PAC that dumps millions into Democrat campaigns in the Lone Star state is under a Department of Justice (DOJ) investigation following a viral undercover video featuring a now-former employee, two sources familiar with the matter confirmed to Fox News Digital. "We are paying people $25 to attend a one-hour Zoom class to learn why voting is important and why the Republicans are causing all these bad things," Sky McAdams, a former organizing manager at the Texas Majority PAC told an undercover reporter in a video obtained by Townhall. "So it's like a roundabout way of paying people for their votes, essentially, which is interesting," said McAdams. When the undercover reporter asked what the program was called, McAdams said it's called the "Paid Relational Program." "I think 'Rally Texas' is the official name," McAdams continued. "You can't pay someone to vote for someone. You can't be like, 'Here's $25, go vote for me.' You can say, 'attend a one-hour class and you can receive $25,' and then the class just talks about, like, the importance of voting." REPUBLICAN CAVALRY ARRIVES FOR KEN PAXTON AS BIG-BUCKS TEXAS OFFENSIVE OPENS CASH FLOODGATES "It's a creative way to kind of... but right now we could use all the help we can get," the reporter says in response. "Yeah, you know, like, if I was a Republican, I'd be pissed. I'd be like, 'that's shady as f---,'" McAdams agreed of the supposed nefarious-ness of the action in his reply. The video has racked up millions of views online, leading to the DOJ probe into the Texas Majority PAC. The Texas Majority PAC was founded by "veterans of Texas campaigns" Jason Lee, Katherine Fischer and Crystal Zermeño. The group's mission is to turn Texas permanently blue. According to Transparency USA, by the end of Q2, the PAC had raised nearly $10 million in the 2026 election cycle, and has spent nearly $9 million. It reportedly had more than $1.3 million in cash on hand. A spokesperson for the PAC, Eddie Vale, told Fox News Digital that the video is real and has not been digitally altered or deceptively edited. He also clarified details about "relational organizing" program described by McAdams in the video. TALARICO SAYS HE 'MISSED THE MARK' AS HE BACKTRACKS ON CONTROVERSIAL WOKE STATEMENTS "We hire Texans to join events where they are taught how to organize their friends and family.," he said. "They encourage their friends and family to turn out and vote and send them regular reminders. They are compensated for their organizing work, just like any other job." "Texas Majority PAC runs a relational organizing program, which for years has been a standard part of every campaign’s playbook," Vale said. "Participants in the program are being paid for grassroots organizing work. The way it was described by one rogue employee is factually incorrect, not how we operate, and they were immediately fired." "We will continue to ensure that everyone who has the legal right to vote is able to do so in the face of never-ending attempts from Texas Republicans to disenfranchise them and bad faith attacks from right-wing media to silence organizations that try to help them," Vale continued. Meanwhile, Texas Democrats are feverishly attempting to rally support for scandal-plagued Senate candidate James Talarico. The left-wing candidate has recently walked back some of his more extreme positions, like support for biological men in women's sports, his previous claims that "God is non-binary" and that there are six sexes. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Talarico is running against Republican state Attorney General Ken Paxton. Despite the fact that Texas is known as a traditionally red state, the outcome could be decided by a razor-thin margin. Neither McAdams nor the Texas Majority PAC returned Fox News Digital's comment requests related to the investigation.

articles.title: GOP lawmaker’s fraud crusade takes dramatic turn as scandal engulfs his own career
articles.summary: Utah State Rep. Trevor Lee, a Republican who championed anti-fraud bills and praised Nick Shirley, now faces mortgage fraud charges himself.
articles.body: After spending years railing against fraud, Utah Republican state Rep. Trevor Lee has resigned after being charged with fraud himself. The Utah Attorney General's Office filed criminal charges against Lee on Monday, accusing him of forging documents and engaging in fraud in order to obtain a home loan. Prior to the charges, Lee had pushed legislation aimed at combating unemployment fraud and publicly praised efforts to expose the sweeping fraud scandals that have rocked Minnesota in recent years. In one video obtained by prosecutors, the CEO of a Utah water company "stated that Lee had requested cash advances totaling $93,000 to show increased income to assist in purchasing his home, and that Lee said he would make (the CEO) 'whole' by securing (his) company a government contract with Hill Air Force Base," according to the charging document. SWING-STATE'S FRAUD RECKONING RAISES MINNESOTA-STYLE ALARM AS WILD SCHEMES EXPOSED Another company claimed that Lee improperly used an offer letter from them to make it seem as if his income was higher than it was. "Lee devised a scheme to obtain a $1 million home loan by false pretenses. To execute it, he communicated fraudulent documents to Kind Lending through the mortgage process — a forged Enevive employment contract, a loan application overstating his Enevive income, and a Blue Logic offer letter he knew misrepresented his employment," prosecutors wrote. Investigators say Lee admitted during an interview that he personally forged the Enevive CEO’s signature on the employment contract to obtain the loan and knew the offer letter did not reflect income the company could actually pay him. EXCLUSIVE: NICK SHIRLEY FIRES BACK AT MINNESOTA CRITICS: 'NUMBERS DON'T LIE, AND CONVICTIONS DON'T LIE' Lee’s social media feed is full of positive references to Nick Shirley, a content creator who attracted national attention after releasing videos alleging fraud involving Somali-run childcare centers and other publicly funded programs in Minnesota. "Nick is going to stop a Gavin Newsom presidency single handily (sic.)," Lee said in one post.
